articles.title: B/R Experts Week 6 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: We're five weeks into the 2026 NFL season, and for everything we know, there are two things we do not.
articles.body:
We're five weeks into the 2026 NFL season, and for everything we know, there are two things we do not.

We know that the San Francisco 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs are good. We know that the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans are bad. We know that teams like the Atlanta Falcons and Pittsburgh Steelers fall somewhere in-between.

However, exactly zero people predicted that five weeks in that the Minnesota Vikings would be one of the three remaining undefeated teams. Or that the Los Angeles Chargers would still be searching for their first victory. Or that the New York Giants would be in first place in the NFC East.

Never mind that outside the aforementioned Vikings, the entire NFC North would be filled with teams that look awesome one week and awful the next.

It all goes to show that the old axiom "any given Sunday" is as true as ever. And after another wild and wacky week of NFL action, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have come together to comb through the chaos and rank the NFL's 32 teams.

The bookends are the same as a week ago. What's in-between though?

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NO | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

The story remains the same five weeks into the 2026 NFL campaign. The Miami Dolphins are the NFL's least-talented and worst team.

How bad are they? According to The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia , Miami ranks dead last in offensive success rate for any squad over the last five seasons.

The Dolphins' struggles aren't surprising. Malik Willis is in his first season as a full-time starting quarterback. Miami features the league's worst wide receiver depth. Running back De'Von Achane suffered a season-ending injury. The offensive line isn't playing particularly well, either.

Let's call it what it is: This season is a transition year for the Dolphins. Everything is going according to plan from that perspective. -- Sobleski

It's any given Sunday in the NFL, but the Tennessee Titans are a basement-dwelling team that hasn't scored more than 20 points in a game this season. It'll be difficult for them to earn their first victory with an impotent offense.

Rookie wideout Carnell Tate showed signs of development, but the Houston Texans held him to one catch for six yards.

Tennessee's two play-callers, defensive-minded head coach Robert Saleh and offensive coordinator Brian Daboll, will keep searching for answers. -- Moton

It's strange to call a season lost in October, but it already feels like the Los Angeles Chargers should be looking toward 2027 and beyond. Justin Herbert has significantly regressed in Mike McDaniel's offense, while Los Angeles' defense has been uncharacteristically mistake-prone for a Jim Harbaugh team.

Unfortunately, injuries are beginning to mount for the second straight season, too.

No NFL team has ever gone from 0-5 and made the playoffs, and Los Angeles sure doesn't look like a squad capable of becoming the first. If the Chargers remain winless entering their Week 7 bye—which is extremely possible with a trip to Kansas City up next—we could see some shake-ups during the off week.

Harbaugh has publicly voiced his support for McDaniel, but it's fair to wonder if L.A. will continue to support Harbaugh if the team continues to stumble. -- Knox

The Arizona Cardinals' new coaching staff turned Marvin Harrison Jr. into an afterthought, then traded him to the Houston Texans. The Cardinals should embrace the role of sellers and trade veterans who aren't part of their long-term plan.

At 1-4, with that one victory over the winless Los Angeles Chargers, the Cardinals should start thinking about what they want their roster to look like for next season. Arizona is going nowhere in 2026. -- Moton

Jalon Daniels opened eyes with his performance Thursday during his first road start in Dallas for a primetime contest.

After an 0-4 start, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers could have easily gone into cruise control with Baker Mayfield out of the lineup due to injury. Instead, Todd Bowles' squad responded with a resounding victory.

Daniels was particularly impressive. The undrafted rookie showed a level of maturity and play-making ability that validated the coaching staff's decision to anoint him as QB2. Granted, the Cowboys defense remains rudderless and the unit still has significant issues on that side of the ball. Even so, Daniels completed 76 percent of his passes and didn't make any major mistakes--which is exactly what a team wants from any backup in that situation, whether they are a rookie or not. -- Sobleski

Week 5 Result: Tied vs. New York Giants 27-27

This writer isn't going to say that the Commanders should fire head coach Dan Quinn now. That isn't going to save what appears to be another lost season in the nation's capital.

For a coach who is supposedly a defensive guy, Quinn's unit, um, stinks. The Commanders were 26th in the league in pass defense entering Week 5, and that number isn't getting any better after Jameis Winston carved them up.

There's also the horrible clock management in overtime, Jayden Daniels deserves blame there as well, but it's on the coach to be sure his quarterback knows he can't go down in bounds. Last I looked, Daniels has a radio in his helmet.

The Commanders need a Ben Johnson. A Liam Coen. A Dave Canales. Someone who can develop Daniels.

Don't write off the Houston Texans yet. Yes, they should've beaten the winless Tennessee Titans, and no, Marvin Harrison Jr. isn't the savior who'll turn the offense into a juggernaut.

However, if the Texans beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London this week, they'll be 2-4, like last season before winning 10 of 11 games. It's a tough feat, but Houston did it with mostly the same players from the previous campaign.

It's not time to jump back on the Texans bandwagon, but a win over the division-leading Jaguars could spark a season turnaround. -- Moton

The Saints provided a glimmer of hope late last season with a four-game winning streak. The optimism that once surrounded this roster and its coaching staff quickly evaporated during the team's 1-4 start, including an ongoing three-game losing streak.

The most depressing aspect of the Saints' current situation is how thoroughly the Vikings defense dominated Kellen Moore's offense. New Orleans may have fielded a top-10 offense entering the contest, but the group had no answers against Brian Flores' play-calling. The Saints managed only 142 yards Sunday.

What looked like an ascending team is now on its heels with a need to respond in the coming weeks. However, New Orleans' doesn't face another team with a losing record (currently) until the weekend before Christmas. -- Sobleski

Two wins through five weeks of play nearly equals all of last season's success. The New York Jets are competitive again. Significant talent can be found throughout the roster. However, this year's second overall draft pick, David Bailey, stole the show Sunday against the Cleveland Browns.

Bailey officially announced his NFL arrival with three sacks and four quarterback hits. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Bailey leads all rookies in pressures (26) and quick pressures (nine) generated.

The Jets have enough young talent and Geno Smith playing well at quarterback to be a difficult opponent for anyone as this season progresses. An above-.500 record isn't out of the equation either. If it doesn't happen, the team has a big offseason ahead of it, with the potential to add significantly more high-level talent, as it did with Bailey. -- Sobleski

The Indianapolis Colts' silver lining in their loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers is that they didn't let wideout DK Metcalf put together a highlight performance after his dismissive comments toward cornerback Sauce Gardner.

Nonetheless, the Colts must sort out their defensive issues, and it goes beyond Gardner allowing a 112.2 passer rating in coverage. The Colts gave up 127 rushing yards to the Steelers, who entered Week 5 with the 22nd-ranked rushing offense.

The Colts are stuck in mediocrity, though they can get back to .500 with a home win over the Tennessee Titans before a two-week road trip against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings and AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars. -- Moton

Remember when the Dallas Cowboys were going to be better defensively this season?

The Cowboys are cooked. Again. And an abysmal defense is the reason why. Playing against a winless Tampa bay Buccaneers team starting an undrafted rookie at quarterback, the Cowboys gave 419 total yards and over 240 yards on the ground. The Cowboys knew exactly what Tampa Bay was going to do—and there was nothing they could do to stop it.

Once again, Dallas is at the bottom of the league in total defense. They can't stop the run, allowing almost 170 yards per game. The pass defense is better, but still below average.

Joey Porter Jr. isn't going to fix things. Neither will another trade.

The more things change in Big D, the more they stay the same. -- Davenport

Just when the Atlanta Falcons looked like they were getting on track and had an answer at the game's most important position, Michael Penix Jr. suffered another injury and couldn't finish Sunday's contest against the Baltimore Ravens.

The severity of Penix's injury is not yet known, though he will get imaging on a rib this week.

Considering Penix's history, another injury has to be demoralizing, even if it's not a major problem. He's now suffered three ACL tears and had surgery on both of his shoulders. He can't stay on the field, which has affected his development. The Falcons have too much talent to be constantly worrying whether they're projected starter is going to be in the lineup. Tua Tagovailoa didn't help his case by throwing an interception to end overtime and hand the Ravens a victory. -- Sobleski

Week 5 Result: Lost vs. Jacksonville 19-17 (London)

The Philadelphia Eagles are no strangers to adversity. The team is battle-tested. But the Eagles are also in trouble.

Philly's offense was already struggling to move the ball consistently before running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith went down and the team lost two starters on the offensive line. That offense now is stagnant. Stuck.

The defense has issues as well. Defensive tackle Jalen Carter was a force in London, but the Eagles aren't generating pressure off the edge. Philadelphia has been ahead late in each of the last two games—and lost them both.

Philly now has a two-game homestand to try to right the ship, but next week's visit from the Carolina Panthers is no gimme.

If the Eagles fall to 2-4, keep the kids and Philly away from sports talk radio.

Week 5 Result: Tied at Washington 27-27 (OT)

On one hand, the New York Giants have just one fewer win than they did all of last season after just five weeks. Not only are the G-Men in first place, but they are 1.5 games clear of every other team in the NFC Least.

The Giants were also down two scores to a one-win Commanders team before engineering a furious comeback. The Giants turned the ball over twice, including a backbreaking fumble in overtime when they were in field goal range. If Jayden Daniels could tell time, the Giants would be 3-2.

The reality is that the one good team the Giants played this year blew them out. But the scheduling reality is that New York doesn't play another good team until they face the Jaguars—on November 22.

Is this a playoff-caliber team? Probably not. Could it make the postseason anyway?

Week 5 Result: Lost at New England 45-17

Even after consecutive losses, the Las Vegas Raiders are sitting at 3-2. Most Raiders fans would have taken that sort of start to the season, given the option to do so in August. However, things feel a lot different after a blowout loss to the New England Patriots than they felt following last week's close loss to the rival Chiefs.

Playing across the country with a less-than-100-percent Ashton Jeanty certainly didn't help Las Vegas. However, the Raiders' defense looked legitimately bad for the first time this season, and the lack of wide-receiver depth was glaring as Las Vegas tried to keep pace with Drake Maye and Co.

Fernando Mendoza made his 2026 debut after the game got out of hand on Sunday. While Kirk Cousins wasn't benched for performance reasons, calls for Mendoza will intensify if Las Vegas has many more team performances like the one it had in Week 5. -- Knox

Week 5 Result: Lost at New York Jets 17-12

The Cleveland Browns are who we thought they were—a few weeks ago.

To their credit, the Browns briefly held the lead in the fourth quarter Sunday. The defense is keeping the team in games week after week. But the offense is trash—plain and simple.

Facing a Jets defense that the Chicago Bears dominated a week ago, the Browns did next to nothing. Bad weather or no, the Browns managed just 198 yards of offense. There were no running lanes. Deshaun Watson was dropped a whopping eight times.

After three straight wins, it was an ugly, mistake-filled effort. And while next week's AFC North meeting with the team that used to the Browns isn't a must-win, it sort of is if the Browns want to be taken at all seriously in 2026. – Davenport

It's hard to decipher just how good the Detroit Lions can be, even if we know exactly what sort of team they are.

Detroit's offense can look like the league's best when everything is clicking, but its defense is one of the league's worst by just about every metric. The defense did enough against the one-win Cardinals for the Lions to comfortably cruise to 3-2. However, Detroit has to find defensive answers during next week's bye if it hopes to match points with the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings in its next two games.

The Lions should be prime candidates to trade for defensive help in the coming weeks. -- Knox

The NFL is a results-driven business. And in that regard it was mission accomplished for the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5—after dropping two straight the team got back on track in the Queen City.

However, even in victory there was cause for concern—on both sides of the ball.

Offensively, the Bengals had 117 yards on the ground, but it took 31 carries to get there. However, that 117 yards was over 40 yards above their season average, and Cincy may have found something in getting Samaje Perine more involved on the ground.

Defensively, Cincinnati's new-look unit has looked more like last year's squad—and that ain't a compliment. Allowing 24 points to a sputtering offense that was averaging a league-low 11.5 points per game is not a good look.

The Bengals are no doubt glad to be 3-2. But there are things to work on over the bye week. – Davenport

Week 5 Result: Won vs. Indianapolis 34-22

The Pittsburgh Steelers are like Jason Voorhees—just when you think they are finally dead, they rise out of the Monongahela River and start chopping people up.

Granted, the Indianapolis Colts are the equivalent of the teenager who hides in a dark shed instead of driving away—Indy is a flawed team. But one week after an uneven outing in Cleveland, the Steelers took care of business, riding an efficient game from quarterback Aaron Rodgers and 188 total yards and two scores from running back Jaylen Warren to their third victory of the season.

The thing is, the Steelers have a chance to build some momentum here. The next two weeks feature winnable matchups with the 1-4 New Orleans Saints and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. That could set the Steelers up at a solid 5-2 when the Browns come calling on Week 8.

Pittsburgh ain't dead just yet. – Davenport

The Carolina Panthers didn't need to do a thing this past weekend to move into sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Currently, Carolina is the only team in the division without a losing record. Plus, the Panthers' next two opponents currently own losing records, with two weeks to specifically prepare for the Philadelphia Eagles.

As always, the bye week provides an opportunity for a roster to get healthy. Carolina could receive significant boosts with defensive Jaelan Phillips, rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling, guard Damien Lewis and wide receiver Jalen Coker likely back after being dinged in recent weeks. Veteran right tackle Taylor Moton and defensive lineman Tershawn Wharton may be taken off injured reserve as well. -- Sobleski

The Green Bay Packers did not look particularly good in the first month of the season. They scraped by the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers but largely looked average during their 2-2 start. However, Green Bay looked like an actual playoff threat during Sunday's win over the rival Chicago Bears.

The Packers' defense still has issues, especially up front, and Green Bay desperately needs to find a way to improve its rushing attack. Yet, the Packers can still be difficult to stop when Jordan Love, Christian Watson, and the passing attack get to clicking.

Love repeatedly dissected the Bears' secondary in Week 5, and he'll have a chance to keep cutting through defenses with the Dallas Cowboys, Detroit Lions, and Carolina Panthers on tap. -- Knox

The Chicago Bears looked like one of the NFC's top contenders in the first month of the season, but Sunday's blowout loss should serve as a wake-up call.

The Bears' defense played extremely well in Weeks 2-4, but it returned to the putrid form we saw in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Playing without quarterback Caleb Williams and running back Kyle Monangai, Chicago had little hope of keeping pace once Green Bay's passing attack got going.

It now feels like those good performances against the Minnesota Vikings, Philadelphia Eagles, and New York Jets may have been a mirage. The Bears need Williams back behind center, and they need their offense to meet Ben Johnson's preseason expectations if Chicago is going to win consistently against playoff-caliber teams. -- Knox

After a suspect start to the season, the New England Patriots have found their way and once again look like the team that represented the AFC in last season's Super Bowl.

A win against the Buffalo Bills proved an impressive turnaround after being trounced by the Jacksonville Jaguars. A letdown could have occurred after an important win over a division rival. Instead, the Patriots responded with a dominant victory over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Drake Maye's about-face after a horrific start to the campaign shows how resilient the 24-year-old quarterback is. The third-year signal-caller established new season-highs Sunday with 374 passing yards and four touchdown passes. More importantly, he didn't turn the ball over for the first time this season. -- Sobleski

Wins can make a lot of problems seem trivial, but the Denver Broncos' offensive issues may not simply go away. Head coach Sean Payton took back play-calling duties from coordinator Davis Webb ahead of Week 5, but the results were largely the same.

Fortunately, in Sunday's win over the rival Chargers, Denver's defense looked a lot more like the top-tier unit the Broncos fielded in 2025. It repeatedly kept points off the board, generated sacks, and forced turnovers that put the offense in scoring position.

If the Broncos' defense can build on what it accomplished in Week 5, it will give Denver chances to stack wins. However, the offense has to start finding answers soon. The 224 total yards it compiled on Sunday were the fewest the Chargers have surrendered all season.

Both units will be heavily tested on Thursday night when the Seattle Seahawks come to town. -- Knox

The Los Angeles Rams have been surprisingly inconsistent in the first four weeks of the season. But if the Rams beat the Buffalo Bills on Monday, they'll have back-to-back wins and midseason momentum that could help them climb back into the top five of these power rankings.

Based on their 2024 matchup, which ended 44-42, these teams should be fun to watch Monday night. -- Moton

Week 5 Result: Won at Atlanta 30-23 (OT)

Good teams find a way to overcome adversity. To win when not at their best. The Ravens did the first in beating a hot Falcons team on the road last night. But in some ways they were at their best in doing so.

With two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson on the shelf with an injured ankle, Baltimore played Ravens football, gouging the league's best run defense entering Week 5 for 208 yards. But when backup quarterback Tyler Huntley had to make plays, "Snoop" was on the case—over 200 passing yards, two touchdowns, another score on the ground and a passer rating of 111.6. He also led Baltimore on a two-minute drive to force overtime.

At 4-1, the Ravens are a game clear of the rest of the AFC North. And while Baltimore would no doubt like Jackson back out there against the Browns in Week 6, the Ravens just showed that they can win without him. – Davenport

Week 5 Result: Lost vs. San Francisco 32-29

The reigning champions must regroup. The Seattle Seahawks are turning the ball over at an alarming rate—nine giveaways over the last four weeks. Since Sam Darnold returned from injury, he's been part of the problem, throwing five interceptions in his last three outings.

Also, the Seahawks running backs must hold onto the ball. Emanuel Wilson and George Holani fumbled, and the San Francisco 49ers scored touchdowns off both turnovers.

The Seahawks fall out of our top five for the first time this season, though they could get back on the right track with a road win over the Denver Broncos on Thursday. -- Moton

Week 5 Result: Won vs. Philadelphia 19-17 (London)

The Jacksonville/London Jaguars pulled off a late win, though Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni took the blame . Quietly, the Jaguars are one of the league's best, and we have taken note, ranking them within our top five.

The Jaguars are a rock-solid squad that plays complementary football, and they don't beat themselves, a hallmark of well-coached teams. So far this season, Jacksonville has turned the ball over just three times while recording eight takeaways.

The Jaguars are also one of the league's best red-zone operations on offense and defense; they finish drives with six points and keep teams out of their end zone. Aside from Brian Thomas Jr.'s disappearing act, there's little to criticize about the Jaguars. -- Moton

Not that long ago ( Week 4 ), the Bills sat atop these Power Rankings. Now, a loss in Los Angeles Monday night would drop the team out of first place in the AFC East.

Regardless of what happens in this matchup with the Rams, Buffalo is a Super Bowl contender. The team has been for years. But some of the same flaws that have made Josh Allen the quarterback with the most playoff wins to never play in a Super Bowl are back in 2026—particularly on defense, where Buffalo has allowed the sixth-most yards and the seventh-most points in the league per game.

A road win over a quality opponent would assuage some of those doubts. A loss reinforces them.

The Minnesota Vikings moved to 5-0 on Sunday, and for the first time this season, things seemed to be clicking in all phases.

Having Justin Jefferson back in the lineup was huge, and it helped Kyler Murray deliver his best performance as a Viking so far. Aaron Jones returned from a first-quarter knee injury and ran for 113 yards, while Minnesota's defense held the New Orleans Saints to a mere 142 total yards.

The Vikings' defense has looked championship-caliber all season. If Murray and the offense can continue to make positive strides after next week's bye, this team could remain undefeated for the foreseeable future. -- Knox

The Kansas City Chiefs entered their Week 5 bye looking very much like the type of squad that has given the AFC fits in recent years.

Not everything has been perfect. The Chiefs have been relying on undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle, and they just placed Tyquan Thornton on injured reserve. Kansas City narrowly avoided close calls against the Colts and the Raiders en route to their 4-0 start.

Still, this undefeated team with a healthy Patrick Mahomes behind center that entered Week 5 ranked fifth in scoring and sixth in points allowed. -- Knox

The San Francisco 49ers won't move in our power rankings. They were No. 1 last week, and then went on the road to knock off the reigning Super Bowl champions.

This past offseason, the 49ers signed Mike Evans, who hasn't aged past his prime. The Seattle Seahawks pass defense gave up the fewest yards entering Week 5, yet it couldn't stop the 33-year-old, who caught seven passes for 113 yards and a touchdown.

Deebo Samuel Sr. suffered a hamstring injury in the second half. So, the 49ers may need to bring in reinforcements at receiver. Despite the cluster of injuries at that position, they're the best team in the NFL. -- Moton

articles.title: Predicting 2026 NFL Award Winners and Top Darkhorse Candidates After Week 5
articles.summary: With most of Week 5 in the books, we have enough of a sample size to discuss front-runners and dark-horse candidates for NFL Honors awards.
articles.body:
With most of Week 5 in the books, we have enough of a sample size to discuss front-runners and dark-horse candidates for NFL Honors awards.

Of course, players on winning teams will get most of the mentions, but this past Sunday, an edge-rusher on a 2-3 club made a strong case to lead the Defensive Rookie of the Year candidates.

These projections will change as the year progresses, but let's take an early look at the top-performing players and coaches leading teams to strong starts this season.

League MVP: QB Brock Purdy, San Francisco 49ers

After Week 5, Brock Purdy leads the NFL with 13 touchdown passes and an 89.2 QBR.

In the 49ers' competitive matchups, Purdy played at a high level. He threw for two touchdowns without an interception against the Denver Broncos in Week 4. This past Sunday, against the Seattle Seahawks, Purdy turned the ball over, but he engineered two go-ahead scoring drives in the fourth quarter, one for a touchdown and another for a field goal.

Also, keep in mind that the 49ers have lost multiple wide receivers to injuries, including Deebo Samuel Sr., who suffered a hamstring injury in the second half of the previous game. Mike Evans has also been battling a rib injury.

Yet Purdy is still one of the league's top passers and deserves recognition for his numbers despite an undermanned receiving corps.

Dark-Horse Candidate: QB Trevor Lawrence, Jacksonville Jaguars

Trevor Lawrence is off to a strong start, throwing for 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. He's improved his efficiency, completing a career-high 67.1 percent of his passes, and is on pace for a season-high 30 touchdown passes. Following Week 5, FanDuel has listed him fourth among MVP candidates with +900 odds.

Offensive Player of the Year: RB Jahmyr Gibbs, Detroit Lions

Jahmyr Gibbs is the focal point of the No. 1-scoring offense with a league-leading 747 scrimmage yards and nine total touchdowns. He's coming off a season-high 207 scrimmage yards against the Arizona Cardinals and looks to be well on his way to his first All-Pro season.

This past offseason, the Detroit Lions traded running back David Montgomery to the Houston Texans, breaking up his Sonic-and-Knuckles connection with Gibbs. Head coach Dan Campbell told reporters that the latter would be the team's bell cow running back, and it's panned out, with backup tailback Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve.

The Lions have fully unleashed Gibbs, and he's posting monster stat lines as their workhorse running back.

Dark-Horse Candidate: WR Christian Watson, Green Bay Packers

Without Josh Jacobs, who's on the commissioner's exempt list, the Packers have leaned heavily on their aerial attack, ranking 10th in pass attempts and last in total carries. As a result, Christian Watson has emerged as a big-time playmaker, catching a team-leading 26 passes for 474 yards and six touchdowns, ranking fifth and second leaguewide in the latter two categories.

Wideout Jayden Reed suffered a season-ending neck injury in Week 2, thinning the Packers' receiving corps. Watson has absorbed more targets and has topped 142 receiving yards in two games, scoring two touchdowns in each.

Defensive Player of the Year: EDGE Will Anderson Jr., Houston Texans

The Houston Texans defense isn't as dominant as last year's unit, but Will Anderson Jr. remains an elite pass-rusher and disruptor off the edge. He leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks and 10 tackles for loss.

As the 2023 Defensive Rookie of the Year, two-time Pro Bowler and 2025 first-team All-Pro, Anderson has established himself as a premier edge-rusher. At his current rate of production, he could join the ranks of Myles Garrett and T.J. Watt as a Defensive Player of the Year winner.

Dark-Horse Candidate: EDGE Dallas Turner, Minnesota Vikings

Someone must represent the Vikings' No. 1-ranked scoring defense. While we can make the case for cornerback Byron Murphy Jr., who has five pass breakups and three interceptions for the No. 3 pass defense, Dallas Turner gets the nod as he continues to blossom into a top-tier pass-rusher.

Turner is on pace to shatter his career highs of eight sacks and 24 pressures from last season. He's recorded 5.5 sacks and 22 pressures in five games. The Vikings are headed into a Week 6 bye, so Turner will fall in total counting stat categories, but he's someone to keep an eye on if Minnesota's defense continues to shut down opponents.

Offensive Rookie of the Year: WR Denzel Boston, Cleveland Browns

As one of the biggest surprises early in the season, the Cleveland Browns are 3-2 with a young core. Rookie second-rounder Denzel Boston is already a rising star in the Browns' youth movement, and he's the clear-cut top receiver in Cleveland's passing offense.

Boston has caught 16 passes for 330 yards and three touchdowns. At 6'4", 215 pounds, he's an imposing playmaker who can match up against physical defensive backs and box out defenders in the red zone. Boston went seventh among receivers in this year's class, but he's the most productive through five weeks.

Dark-Horse Candidate: WR Antonio Williams, Washington Commanders

Antonio Williams hasn't garnered much buzz, but he's third among rookie wideouts with 155 receiving yards and scored a touchdown in his regular-season debut.

Williams is third on Washington's receiver depth chart, but Terry McLaurin (31) and Stefon Diggs (32) have each missed one game. As older receivers, they could miss more time as the year progresses. If so, Williams could emerge as a starting receiver in a solid role.

The Commanders' 30th-ranked scoring defense will force them to throw a lot, which may inflate their receivers' numbers. Even in a complementary role, Williams' stats could look impressive in a pass-heavy offense.

Defensive Rookie of the Year: EDGE David Bailey, New York Jets

In Week 5, David Bailey had a breakout game, registering seven tackles (five solo) and three sacks. According to Next Gen Stats , he tied 2024 Defensive Rookie of the Year Jared Verse for the most pressures—nine—in a single game.

Bailey leads all rookies and the Jets with five sacks and should reach double digits for the season. Regardless of how Gang Green's season pans out, he should be the front-runner for this award. The Texas Tech product's impact on passing and rushing downs stands out.

Dark-Horse Candidate: CB Hezekiah Masses, Las Vegas Raiders

The Las Vegas Raiders may have a late-round gem in Hezekiah Masses. The rookie fifth-rounder capitalized on an opportunity when 2025 third-rounder Darien Porter sat out with an injury in Week 2.

In Porter's absence, Masses recorded two interceptions in the Raiders' win over the Los Angeles Chargers and has kept the starting job. He leads the rookie class with three interceptions and six pass breakups. That said, Masses must rebound from a rough Week 5 outing in New England.

Comeback Player of the Year: QB Patrick Mahomes, Kansas City Chiefs

With running back Kenneth Walker III in the fold, the Kansas City Chiefs don't need Patrick Mahomes to carry the offense, but he's still efficient from the pocket, throwing for nine touchdowns and two interceptions with a 64.1 percent completion rate.

In his first game back from a torn ACL, Mahomes signaled that he's healthy with a 15-yard rushing touchdown in the 2026 season opener against the Denver Broncos. Since Week 1, he's logged only five rush attempts, though the two-time first-team All-Pro leads the ninth-ranked passing attack.

Dark-Horse Candidate: QB Michael Penix Jr., Atlanta Falcons

The Atlanta Falcons are 2-3, but they're a much better team when Michael Penix Jr. starts and finishes games. After an 0-2 start with journeyman Cooper Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand under center, the Falcons won consecutive outings with Penix, blowing out the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints by 21-plus points in road games.

Unfortunately, Penix didn't finish this past Sunday's game with the Baltimore Ravens because of a rib injury. On a positive note, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported there's "optimism" that the Falcons signal-caller could play in Week 6 against the Chicago Bears.

In three games, Penix has thrown for 719 yards, three touchdowns and an interception with a 67.5 percent completion rate.

Coach of the Year: Kyle Shanahan, San Francisco 49ers

Somehow, Kyle Shanahan has never won Associated Press Coach of the Year, but he may finally get the award after this season.

The San Francisco 49ers are 5-0, and they've obliterated three of their opponents, including the Los Angeles Rams, who entered the season as a popular Super Bowl favorite. Don't let the 36-30 final score in their Week 3 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals fool you. The Cardinals racked up points in garbage time. Though the 49ers had a competitive battle with the Denver Broncos in Week 4, they still won by 10.

This past Sunday, San Francico knocked off the reigning champions to take the lead spot in the NFC West.

Keep in mind that the 49ers are doing this without five-time Pro Bowl pass-rusher Nick Bosa and a wide receiver corps decimated with injuries. Shanahan has been a top-tier head coach for a decade, and he may get well-deserved recognition if the 49ers stay atop the standings.

Dark-Horse Candidate: Liam Coen, Jacksonville Jaguars

The Jaguars don't garner a ton of media attention. They have back-to-back games in London, which has kept them out of the headlines.

That said, if not for a Week 2 fourth-quarter letdown against the Broncos, Jacksonville would be undefeated. Jacksonville led for most of that game and allowed two touchdown drives within 12 minutes of regulation.

Still, the Jaguars are one of the league's best teams with the 12th-ranked scoring attack and a defense giving up the second-fewest points. If Liam Coen leads the club to back-to-back AFC South titles, he deserves a mention for Coach of the Year.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Watch Sam Cosmi Kick Pylon in Trending Video After Commanders' Stunning Tie vs. Giants
articles.summary: Nobody on the Washington Commanders was particularly happy after the team botched the final play in overtime against the New York Giants, allowing the clock to run out and preventing a potential game-winning field-goal attempt.
articles.body:
Nobody on the Washington Commanders was particularly happy after the team botched the final play in overtime against the New York Giants, allowing the clock to run out and preventing a potential game-winning field-goal attempt.

Offensive lineman Sam Cosmi took his frustrations out on a goal-line pylon:

The Commanders had driven the ball to the New York Giants' 25-yard line with just 15 seconds left in overtime, well in range for a Drew Stevens field goal. But Washington chose to run another play, ostensibly for one of three reasons—to either get a bit closer, get the ball to Stevens' preferred hash or to run the clock as far down as possible to ensure the Giants didn't get the ball in the event of a miss.

But quarterback Jayden Daniels took a sack after an odd scramble and, with the team's receivers running down the field and the rest of Washington's players taking their time getting reset, the clock ran down to zero. It appeared that Daniels and his teammates thought they had a timeout remaining.

It was an unmitigated disaster, costing Washington a win and dropping its record to just 1-3-1 on the season.

"We've just got to communicate that, that's the whole thing," Daniels told reporters when asked if he was aware the team lacked a timeout. "It starts with me, communicating to the whole offense in the huddle. And I think everybody will say that from the top down."

"That last sequence... throw it out of bounds, clock it, give yourself a chance to kick," head coach Dan Quinn added. "We pride ourselves on those moments at the end of games. And after the first-down run, still trying to gain more for the kick, and the right call honestly is that we can go clock it early. Don't put ourselves in that spot. And that's my responsibility, nobody else's."

From the coaching staff to the players on the field, it was one of the worst clock-management situations you'll ever see, costing Washington a much-needed win.

articles.title: Deebo Samuel Injury, Latest on 49ers WR's Timeline to Return After Exiting vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: A key member of the San Francisco 49ers' offense will have to miss some time after an injury on Sunday.
articles.body:
A key member of the San Francisco 49ers' offense will have to miss some time after an injury on Sunday.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that wide receiver Deebo Samuel is expected to miss "at least a couple of weeks" following a hamstring injury suffered against the Seattle Seahawks.

Samuel exited Sunday's game in the second half after stepping awkwardly while trying to make a play. He fumbled in the process and was helped off the field and into the locker room.

The 49ers went on to beat the defending champions 32-29 to remain perfect on the season.

Samuel finished the game with two receptions for 21 yards, adding a pair of carries for four yards. The veteran receiver is up to 206 receiving yards, 78 rushing yards and three touchdowns so far in his first season back with San Francisco.

Samuel, 30, was traded to the Washington Commanders ahead of the 2025 campaign but returned to the Niners in free agency over the summer. The former All-Pro receiver is looking to help San Francisco in its quest for a Super Bowl, but he'll have to spend a few weeks on the sideline.

With Samuel set to miss some time, and plenty of other players still working their way back from injuries, the 49ers will need second-string receiver Jordan Watkins to step up. The second-year player has just two receptions for 60 yards in three games, but he'll surely get more targets in the coming weeks.

Luckily for San Francisco, veteran receiver Mike Evans has put together a strong year with 326 yards and three touchdowns, including a performance on Sunday that included 113 yards and a touchdown.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian’s ‘Joe Smith’ argument for Arch Manning is absolute nonsense for an average QB
articles.summary: Arch Manning's inconsistency at Texas raises real questions about whether Steve Sarkisian would have benched a lesser-known quarterback by now.
articles.body: The narrative around Arch Manning at Texas would probably be a tad easier to deal with if head coach Steve Sarkisian would stop adding unnecessary fuel to the fire. We all understand whether the Longhorns quarterback receives a lot more attention than others across the country based off his last name alone, that's a given. But, at some point folks have got to start putting realistic expectations on the guy who is leading the Texas offense. COLLEGE FOOTBALL MEGA ROSTERS AREN'T DELIVERING A RETURN ON INVESTMENT AS LSU, TEXAS A&M AND OREGON ARE PROVING Right now, Arch Manning is a good college quarterback, and at times he plays like an average passer who has cost his team at least one game this season. Throw in the fact that he's the face of Texas football right now, and obviously there could be moments that the latest Manning quarterback is feeling the pressure. My goodness though, his head coach is not doing him any favors from a public perception standpoint. If this was 'Joe Smith', the Texas football team might be playing a different QB On Monday, Steve Sarkisian was asked by a reporter that if you took the name 'Manning' off the back of his jersey, would there not be all of the 'incredible' expectations on the quarterback. After starting his answer with the cliché talk of this being a team game, which it is, and the scheme of running the Texas offense, Sarkisian delivered this gem of an answer. ARCH MANNING RANKED FIFTH AMONG 2027 NFL DRAFT QUARTERBACKS AS EXEC QUESTIONS 'BLIND FAITH' BASED OFF NAME "I think if you took the name off the back of his jersey and you said 'here's Joe Smith playing quarterback at the University of Texas and here's a guy that's beaten four top-10 ranked teams in his last thirteen starts' we'd be praising the guy," Sarkisian noted. "The expectations are high for him, but he understands that. The expectations are high for all of us. So, we gotta put our nose back to the grind and get back to work." UNRANKED OKLAHOMA KNOCKS OFF NO. 1 TEXAS IN WALK-OFF FASHION AFTER ARCH MANNING'S ROUGH 4TH QUARTER For the love of all that's good, save us with this nonsense. If Manning was actually named 'Joe Smith', Steve Sarkisian would have already given the backup quarterbacks at least a shot at overtaking Arch Manning as the starter. The reality is that Arch has been very inconsistent at Texas, and that's ok. He's not going to wow the audience every week, which is something everyone in college football should recognize by now. NO. 1 TEXAS ESCAPES TENNESSEE WITH THRILLING SEC VICTORY AS PRESIDENT TRUMP WATCHES ON FROM NEYLAND STADIUM Also, the Longhorns should feel lucky that they don't have three losses on the season already, given that fourth-quarter performance by Ohio State and Tennessee's lack of offensive firepower outside of its rushing attack. Arch is getting no favors from Sarkisian, but the quarterback is not a first-rounder. We have now reached the point of trying to make sense of Arch Manning being an average college football quarterback by using his popularity as a reason for why he takes so much heat when things go wrong. It should just come down to the fact that if this were any other school or situation, Arch Manning is receiving the same type of critique as Josh Hoover at Indiana or Dante Moore at Oregon. ARCH MANNING ISN’T BACKING DOWN FROM EXPECTATIONS, AND NEITHER IS STEVE SARKISIAN, AS CFP SEMIS AREN'T ENOUGH But, since Steve Sarkisian wants to continue giving these types of answers regarding his quarterback, the outcry will only continue to increase if Manning keeps playing like this. ARCH MANNING OFFICIALLY GOES THROUGH THE PR SPIN CYCLE AND THE FINISHED PRODUCT SOUNDS AWFUL No, he doesn’t look like a top-10 NFL Draft pick, or even the top quarterback in this potential class. But sure, let's act as though Manning wouldn’t be receiving this type of criticism if he had a different last name. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There is a reality that if Arch did not have the last name, we might not be talking about him at all in relation with Texas. We could be discussing the starting quarterback for a Group of Six college football team. At some point, Sarkisian has to realize he's not doing his quarterback any favors with these answers.

articles.title: 'Disgusted' Mike Tomlin 'Threw Up' from Cam Skattebo's Fumble, Commanders-Giants Tie
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin knows what winning football looks like from his 19 years as the head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Sunday's game between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants that ended in a 27-27 tie was anything but winning football.
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin knows what winning football looks like from his 19 years as the head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers, and Sunday's game between the Washington Commanders and New York Giants that ended in a 27-27 tie was anything but winning football.

"I'd describe it as disgusting," Tomlin said Sunday during NBC's coverage. "Division wins are too precious in the National Football League. I was disgusted by the Skattebo fumble. I threw up in my mouth a little bit at the end of the game. It's just tough, we'll never know what happened. … Division wins are very precious, and they had one in their hands and let it slip away."

The Cam Skattebo fumble he referenced happened in overtime when all the Giants needed was a field goal to win the game. They were inside the Washington 30-yard line when the running back lost the fumble.

That put Washington in a position where a field goal would win on the other side, and it seemed like it was going to come away with a win when it drove to the New York 24-yard line.

However, Jayden Daniels took a snap, looked confused with the ball in his hands and was tackled in bounds with the clock still running. The Commanders didn't have any timeouts remaining and were unable to line up in time for a spike, which meant the clock expired and the game ended as a tie.

New York's missed field goal on the first possession of overtime was just a preview of what was to come in an overtime that both teams would surely like to forget.

"We've just got to communicate that, that's the whole thing," Daniels told reporters after the game. "It starts with me, communicating to the whole offense in the huddle. And I think everybody will say that from the top down."

Ultimately, the Giants likely feel better about the tie considering the Commanders were in a position to win it without the time mismanagement at the end. But Skattebo's fumble also cost them an opportunity to come away with an NFC East road victory.

New York is still in first place at 3-1-1 as the only team that isn't below .500 in the division. As for the 1-3-1 Commanders, they missed a chance to build some momentum with Daniels returning to the lineup from injury.

That they blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter before that overtime likely just makes it worse.

articles.title: Cowboys Hire Former NFL HC to Defensive Staff amid Struggles with Christian Parker on Hot Seat
articles.summary: Amid a rough start to the 2026 campaign, the Dallas Cowboys are bringing some help to their defensive coaching staff.
articles.body:
Amid a rough start to the 2026 campaign, the Dallas Cowboys are bringing some help to their defensive coaching staff.

Per ESPN's Todd Archer, the team is hiring veteran coach and former head coach of the Cleveland Browns, Mike Pettine, to the defensive staff.

Pettine has been a coach in the NFL since 2002, first working with the Baltimore Ravens before taking over as the New York Jets' defensive coordinator in 2009. He spent a season as the defensive coordinator for the Buffalo Bills in 2013 before landing his first head coaching job with the Browns in 2014.

His sole stint as a head coach didn't go well, as he missed the playoffs in both seasons before being fired after the 2015 campaign.

Pettine was the Green Bay Packers' defensive coordinator from 2018 to 2020, where he worked with Christian Parker, the current defensive coordinator of the Cowboys.

Most recently, Pettine was the assistant head coach and outside linebackers coach of the Minnesota Vikings. He retired from coaching after the 2025 campaign, but will now head back to work for Dallas.

The hiring comes amid a 2-3 start for the Cowboys, whose defense has shown little improvement from last year. Dallas ranks second-to-last in yards allowed per game (395.4) and has given up the seventh-most points per game (27.2).

The team acquired star cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this month, but he missed Thursday's game due to illness. He should be a difference-maker once he settles in, but he may not be enough to completely turn things around for the Cowboys.

After losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week, the Cowboys, joined by their newest coaching hire, will look to get back on track against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

articles.title: Robert Saleh Rips Titans' OL While Cam Ward's Future Questioned as 2027 NFL Draft Order Takes Shape
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh did not hold back when assessing his offensive line after the team dropped to 0-5 with Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh did not hold back when assessing his offensive line after the team dropped to 0-5 with Sunday's 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans.

"It was nowhere near good enough to be qualified as a NFL offensive line," he said Monday, per Teresa M. Walker of the Associated Press.

While much of the focus was on the poor play of quarterback Cam Ward in the immediate aftermath of the loss, the offensive line also struggled. Ward was sacked four times and used his mobility to escape a number of other sacks. Videos of missed assignments went viral on social media.

Monday's comments came after Ward was questioned to the point Saleh told reporters Sunday he was not benching the quarterback

For his part, the Miami product said he's "not a loser" when asked if he was growing accustomed to Tennessee consistently falling short. Ward is now 3-19 as a starter, although the offensive line isn't doing him any favors.

Pro Football Focus ranked Tennessee as the 24th-best offensive line in the league before the Week 5 struggles.

At this point, it is clear the Titans need to make a number of moves before they will once again be competitive in the AFC playoff race. They are one of three teams with an 0-5 record alongside the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers and would be in line for the No. 1 pick if the season ended after the most recent loss.

Whether that means drafting another quarterback remains to be seen, but whoever is under center will need better protection from the offensive line.

articles.title: Dan Quinn still 'furious' about tie with Giants after clock blunder: 'We've got a lot of s*** to clean up'
articles.summary: The Commanders and Giants tied on Sunday after Washington failed to stop the clock and set up a possible game-winning field goal.
articles.body:
Dan Quinn, roughly 24 hours after a brutal mistake cost them a win, is still absolutely livid.

The Washington Commanders head coach, after they failed to stop the clock for a game-winning field goal and ended up tying with the New York Giants on Sunday, said he was "furious" about his team's execution late in the contest.

"We work really hard on these, and it didn't look like that yesterday," he said, via The 33rd Team's Ari Meirov . "I'm pissed about it."

The Commanders, after making it well into field-goal range in the final seconds at Northwest Stadium on Sunday, let time expire in overtime. All they had to do was spike the ball to set up a 41-yard field goal, but Jayden Daniels scrambled instead and didn't leave his team enough time to get another play off.

Quinn erupted on the sidelines, and slammed his headset to the ground before just standing there in disbelief.

Quinn said Monday they wanted to "use some clock after getting into field-goal range" there, even though a made field goal would have ended the game. They handed the ball off to running back Rachaad White, and that play took "entirely too long," he said.

"It was a breakdown. It can't happen," Quinn said. "Our time today as a team was spent on the how and the why and make sure that it never does again. Yesterday's ending was the biggest example, but we've got a lot of s*** to clean up from yesterday's game. "Trust me, everyone in this building, starting with me, feels that urgency."

"It was a breakdown. It can't happen," Quinn said. "Our time today as a team was spent on the how and the why and make sure that it never does again. Yesterday's ending was the biggest example, but we've got a lot of s*** to clean up from yesterday's game.

"Trust me, everyone in this building, starting with me, feels that urgency."

While a lot of things went wrong for Washington, Quinn has taken a big chunk of the criticism in the wake of the loss. As the head coach, that makes sense. But now that he's in his third season with the team, and they are off to just a 1-3-1 start, it has some questioning his job security.

Quinn holds just an 18-20-1 record leading the Commanders. They made it to the playoffs in his first season, but went just 5-12 last year.

Quinn was asked about his job security Monday, and said he had a conversation with owner Josh Harris on Sunday night. That conversation, however, is a regular thing for them.

"Josh and I talk regularly before games, after games, after good games, after tough games. That's a normal process for us," he said, via The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala . "And trust me, no one is pleased with this outcome and where we're at. But the part that we do have, those hard conversations, were asked about where we're at and what we need to fix and what we need to work on. I like having that communication with him."

The Commanders will take on the undefeated San Francisco 49ers next week on Monday night. Though it's still early, Sunday's slip has helped land Quinn and his team in a tough spot after the early stretch of the season.

And, if there are any more self-inflicted mistakes, calls for Quinn's job are sure to get louder.

articles.title: NFL Makes Zxavian Harris Eligibility Decision After DT Attempted to Play for Lane Kiffin, LSU
articles.summary: Zxavian Harris is eligible to play in the NFL after all.
articles.body:
Zxavian Harris is eligible to play in the NFL after all.

While the NFL initially ruled the defensive tackle, who attempted to return to college and play for Lane Kiffin and LSU earlier this year, was not eligible to sign with an NFL team, it changed its mind following an interview with Harris and "independent verification of his activities after the start of NFL training camps."

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer shared the memo the league sent its teams that said Harris "is a free agent and eligible to visit NFL clubs and to sign an NFL player or practice squad contract with any club."

The memo explained the NFL initially ruled him ineligible to sign with a team for the ongoing season "because he had played college football after the opening of NFL training camps."

However, Harris disputed the notion he played collegiately after training camp, which led to the interview with the league and the "independent verification" that led to the NFL confirming he "did not participate in an organized practice with a college football team."

Harris and tight end Dae'Quan Wright generated plenty of headlines earlier this season when they attempted to return to college and play for Kiffin's squad after previously playing for the coach at Ole Miss.

While both players went undrafted, they signed contracts with NFL teams ahead of the 2026 campaign.

Neither appeared in a regular-season game, though.

Their efforts to play for LSU ultimately failed, as the SEC passed a rule preventing players from returning to college. The Tigers also left both players off their active roster when they began the 2026 campaign.

Harris helped lead Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff last season with 58 tackles, nine tackles for loss, three sacks, three passes defended and one interception. He went undrafted but now has an opportunity to continue chasing his NFL dreams following this latest decision.

articles.title: JuJu Smith-Schuster Works Out for Vikings After OBJ Contract, WR Released by Giants in Preseason
articles.summary: After being released by the New York Giants ahead of training camp, JuJu Smith-Schuster could have the chance to suit up for a new team.
articles.body:
After being released by the New York Giants ahead of training camp, JuJu Smith-Schuster could have the chance to suit up for a new team.

Per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the veteran wide receiver worked out with the Minnesota Vikings on Monday. The Vikings previously signed Odell Beckham Jr. to their practice squad following his release from the Giants.

Smith-Schuster, a Pro Bowler in 2018, spent his first five seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers before helping the Kansas City Chiefs win a Super Bowl in 2022. After a stint with the New England Patriots in 2023, he rejoined the Chiefs for the 2024 and 2025 campaigns.

While Smith-Schuster was no longer the player he once was, he managed to make an impact for the Chiefs last year, recording 345 yards and a touchdown in 17 games.

After signing with the Giants in June, he was hoping to find his way onto the 53-man roster, but the team released him in August while he was battling a knee injury. The knee injury, plus his declining production, was enough for New York to want to part ways with him.

The Vikings were without Justin Jefferson last week because of an ankle sprain, but he returned to action against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday and had seven receptions for 79 yards and a touchdown.

The team's second option at receiver, Jordan Addison, is dealing with a hamstring injury that forced him to miss Sunday's matchup, so Minnesota perhaps is looking for some help in the meantime.

Beckham initially signed to the Vikings' practice squad but was elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's game. Smith-Schuster will perhaps look to take a similar path.

articles.title: 49ers Called 'Best Team' in NFL by Seahawks Personnel Despite NFC West Rivalry, Schefter Says
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers defeated the defending champion Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, 32-29, remaining perfect on the season at 5-0.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers defeated the defending champion Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, 32-29, remaining perfect on the season at 5-0.

And that earned them some respect from their NFC West rivals.

"There were people in the Seahawks organization over the weekend saying that the Niners are the best team in football," ESPN's Adam Schefter said during Monday morning's Get Up (0:36 mark). "The best team in football. ... I said to myself, 'Whoa, the Seahawks are pretty good too.' And they said, 'This Niners team is pretty great.'"

The season is young, of course, but the Niners now have wins over the Los Angeles Rams, Denver Broncos and Seahawks to start the 2026 season, three of the four teams from last year's Conference Championship games. That has earned them their due flowers.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Injury Update and Timeline for Bears Star, Ben Johnson Talks QB1 Plans vs. Falcons
articles.summary: Sunday's 31-7 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers made it clear the Chicago Bears are going to need Caleb Williams back under center if they are going to accomplish their long-term goals this season, and the quarterback could return for the upcoming game against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Sunday's 31-7 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers made it clear the Chicago Bears are going to need Caleb Williams back under center if they are going to accomplish their long-term goals this season, and the quarterback could return for the upcoming game against the Atlanta Falcons.

"He's doing a great job progressing, and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there."

Johnson also said "no determination" has been made on the starting quarterback between Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum if Williams cannot play and added , "we have three guys that can win games in this league."

Williams suffered a hamstring injury and was carted off the field during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Bears fans surely feared his season might be over in the immediate aftermath of the injury given the help he needed to get off the field and the cart, but all indications are he will be back sooner rather than later.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday that "all signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field this week for Chicago."

Rapoport also referenced the "strenuous workout" the quarterback underwent ahead of the team's loss to the Packers. It seemed to be an important step to clear, and Johnson's comments didn't indicate there was any type of setback.

Despite the loss to Green Bay, Chicago has done a solid job of treading water without its star quarterback.

Keenum led the Bears to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles by throwing for 247 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions, while Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets by throwing for 268 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception.

But Bagent was so bad during the loss to the Packers at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson turned back to Keenum at the end of the game once the outcome was already well in hand.

It wouldn't be shocking if Keenum started against the Falcons given those performances if Williams cannot play, but Chicago would be much better off with its top signal-caller back in the lineup.

articles.title: Malik Willis Benching Addressed by Dolphins HC After Loss to Bengals to Be 0-5 in NFL Standings
articles.summary: Despite a 0-5 start to the season that has seen quarterback Malik Willis struggle, the Miami Dolphins have no plans to make a change under center.
articles.body:
Despite a 0-5 start to the season that has seen quarterback Malik Willis struggle, the Miami Dolphins have no plans to make a change under center.

Head coach Jeff Hafley addressed whether he would consider starting Kyle McCord over Willis after the bye week, and he gave his stamp of approval to Willis.

"We've played five games and Malik is our quarterback," he told reporters Monday.

Through five games, Willis has thrown for 849 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions, completing 56.2 percent of his passes. He had just 137 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in Sunday's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

"It needs to be better, for sure," Haffley said. "But there's signs of it. There was flashes yesterday in that game, especially when I think about that two-minute drive at the half and some of the things he did at the end of the game where he just looked aggressive and comfortable. We gotta work through that."

Willis was a coveted free agent after a strong four games with the Green Bay Packers last year, but he has struggled to repeat his success with his new team. Despite his struggles, it sounds like his job is safe for now.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce joined global giving campaign at Kansas City's Union Station

articles.title: Eagles' Jalen Hurts shouldn't be blamed for loss to Jaguars
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts shouldn't be blamed for the team's loss.
articles.body:
It hurts to lose a game in the NFL, but it hurts extra hard when you're winning the game with eight seconds left and still lose it. The pun on "hurts" is intended, by the way.

Well, that's exactly what happened to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The team took the lead against the Jacksonville Jaguars toward the very end of the game, only to blow it in the last eight seconds. Even though the Jags were favored to win the game, seeing the Eagles ahead had made it seem like this game was over, but it wasn't.

But there's a silver lining for Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts. He worked with what he had. It's hard to blame him when you look at the lineup and reality.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has a silver lining despite loss to Jags

That's an issue ESPN points out in a piece released on Monday looking at Week 5 NFL matchups . They discuss the Eagles' game and how Hurts worked with the limited offense he had.

"Jalen Hurts did well to help manufacture some offense with a depleted group in the first half," Tim McManus of ESPN notes. "He went 5-of-7 against the blitz before the break -- a troubling issue last week against the Rams -- and hit Darius Cooper for a 61-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter."

He also points out that the "offense was stymied for most of the second half and was in jeopardy of being held scoreless after halftime for the third consecutive game. But Hurts moved the Eagles down the field late, setting up Jake Elliott's go-ahead 48-yarder with eight seconds remaining."

So, don't blame Hurts. He wasn't perfect, but he did what he could, and that's the point McManus is making.

articles.title: Dolphins Discard Signs With NFC Contender
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins have started this season 0-5 and have made a bevy of moves along the bottom edge of their roster to see who might stick. One of the player...
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins have started this season 0-5 and have made a bevy of moves along the bottom edge of their roster to see who might stick.

One of the players they recently discarded has found a gig with a much better squad.

Keith Cooper Jr. was cut by the Dolphins two weeks ago.

On Monday, he signed with the Carolina Panthers to take a spot on their practice squad.

Cooper was part of the roster moves on the same day that De'Von Achane was placed on injured reserve. Miami also released Clelin Ferrell and Jordan Miller that day.

A couple weeks later, Cooper is the first to get a new gig.

At the time of his release, Cooper was the surprising decision of the bunch. He had played in each of the first three games for the Dolphins.

The 6-foot-5, 285-pound Cooper had just one tackle through three games. He wasn't playing a ton, but he was a part of the active roster for Miami's 0-3 start.

He's still just 23 years old and in his second season as an undrafted player after a college career spent at Tulane and Houston.

Cooper was with the Cleveland Browns for just one regular season appearance in 2025.

His age and the fact that Cooper has already gotten into a few NFL games both work in his favor. That could keep him around the fringes of the league for years to come.

Think about Cooper's fortune for a moment. Sure, he had to wait it out and hope he could get a new gig.

But instead of starting Week 6 with a team that's 0-5 and at the bottom of the AFC East, he joins a Panthers team that's 2-2 and actually atop the NFC South.

Carolina won its division last season, albeit with just an 8-9 record, and is trying to do so again. The Panthers are led by quarterback Bryce Young, who is hoping to prove he deserves a long-term contract extension.

Cooper is just signed to the practice squad, so he won't be perfectly secure in that gig for a while. The Panthers could also decide after a few weeks, like the Dolphins, to try something different.

But they seem to have sought him out specifically, and so Cooper will get to work on the practice field to make the contending Panthers better. It's one of the closer NFL locales to Miami, but in terms of on-field status, these teams are a long way away from one another.

articles.title: Commanders Have 'A Lot of S--t to Clean Up' After Tie vs. Giants, Dan Quinn Says amid Hot Seat Buzz
articles.summary: After a disastrous ending to Sunday's game against the New York Giants, Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn stated the obvious.
articles.body:
After a disastrous ending to Sunday's game against the New York Giants, Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn stated the obvious.

"Yesterday's ending was the biggest example, but we've got a lot of s--t to clean up from yesterday's game," Quinn told reporters Monday. "And trust me, everyone in this building, starting with me, feels that urgency."

The Commanders were in field goal range in overtime against the Giants and had the chance to hit a walk-off field goal as long as they stopped the clock in time.

On what would be the last play of the game, Jayden Daniels scrambled and was sacked. Washington tried to get back to the line of scrimmage to spike the ball and set up the field goal, but time expired.

Quinn said that he and the coaches were "furious with the execution" and gave his perspective on what happened.

The game ended in a tie, and the Commanders moved to 1-3-1 instead of 2-3.

A rough start to the season, combined with the way things went on Sunday, perhaps has fans questioning whether Washington should move on from Quinn. He recognizes that those questions come with the job, but added that he talks with team owner Josh Harris regularly.

"I do know how the league goes," he said. "No one is pleased with this outcome."

The Minnesota Vikings continued evaluating their receiving options Monday, working out veteran JuJu Smith-Schuster after their victory over the New Orleans Saints. NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reported the visit, but there is no confirmed signing attached to the workout.

Smith-Schuster brings a resume, having played for the Pittsburgh Steelers, Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots. Pittsburgh selected him in the second round of the 2017 NFL Draft, and he developed into a target early in his career.

His best season came in 2018, when he earned Pro Bowl recognition after recording 111 receptions for 1,426 yards and seven touchdowns. He later helped Kansas City win Super Bowl LVII, giving Minnesota a chance to evaluate a receiver with experience in high-pressure situations.

More recently, Smith-Schuster joined the New York Giants during the offseason but was released before the regular season. A knee issue complicated his preseason, making his current physical condition a component of any evaluation.

For Minnesota, a workout offers information without requiring a roster commitment. The Vikings can assess his movement, route execution and potential fit before determining whether further action makes sense.

The workout raises an intriguing question: Could Smith-Schuster get another NFL opportunity in Minnesota? For now, there's no deal, and the visit alone doesn't mean anyone's job is in danger.

Even after Sunday's win, the Vikings are taking a look at what else is available. Smith-Schuster now has a chance to show he still has something to offer.

The next move belongs to Minnesota: sign him or keep looking.

articles.title: Ball security is an issue for the Giants after fumbling away their chances at Washington
articles.summary: Rallying from down 14 points in the fourth quarter, the New York Giants snatched a stalemate from the jaws of defeat by finishing with a tie at Washington.Bu...
articles.body:
Rallying from down 14 points in the fourth quarter, the New York Giants snatched a stalemate from the jaws of defeat by finishing with a tie at Washington.

But before the Commanders' late-overtime botched clock management ended the game in bizarre fashion, the Giants had a chance to win themselves. Cam Skattebo fumbled the ball away in field-goal range, extending a troubling trend of turnovers.

Counting Jameis Winston's strip-sack late in the second quarter, New York has lost four fumbles through five games. Skattebo, fellow running backs Tyrone Tracy and Najee Harris and Winston each have one.

"You just can't throw your hands up and say, 'Well, we're just not good at it,'" coach John Harbaugh said. "We understand that at some point in time, it becomes unacceptable, but we're not there yet. We've got guys that want to do the right thing, and, as a team, as an offense, we have to get to the point where we protect the football."

Skattebo has fumbled four times on 81 carries. The timing and circumstances of his latest made Skattebo kick himself.

"I'm the player that tries to fight for as many yards as possible for this team," Skattebo said. "I got to make sure I protect the ball for this football team. We win that game if I do."

Still, the Giants are 3-1-1 with 1-4 New Orleans, which has lost three in a row, coming to town Sunday. Unexpected losses by Dallas and Philadelphia have them in sole possession of first place in the NFC East.

"It's a crazy league," Harbaugh said Monday on a video call with reporters. "My wife, she was visiting my daughter and so I was talking to her after the game and she's watching games on TV. And she says, 'The whole NFL is like crazy town right now.' It's crazy town. It's like, there's so much crazy going on in this league right now. That's what makes it so exciting, I guess. And we were right in the middle of it."

Winston is now 3-0 as the starter, winning each game a different way. This time, after completing seven of 16 passes for 72 yards and getting sacked twice in the first half, he was 26 of 38 for 254 and three touchdowns the rest of the way.

"When your back is against the wall, you have to depend on your playmakers," Winston said. "I think we did a good job of doing that: getting the guys the football and mixing (it) up on them, and kind of just threw them off schedule."

The running game still needs to get going. New York had just 103 yards on the ground at Washington and has yet to surpass 170 in a game this season.

J.J. McCarthy was on the field for five snaps. Perhaps offensive coordinator Matt Nagy will be able to get creative in using McCarthy — who is much more mobile than Winston — as a change of pace.

Bryan Hudson is set to make a third consecutive start at center against the Saints. Getting the nod over John Michael Schmitz in Week 4 versus Arizona was a surprise, but now it seems to be Hudson's job.

"He played well," Harbaugh said. "He played well in the game the week before, and he played well in this past game. (There are) things he can do better but (also) things he did really well, and that's what we based it on."

Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada missed three of his five field-goal attempts in rainy conditions Sunday after being 9 of 9 through his first four NFL games. His inaccuracy also affected the play-calling in OT and the decision to have Skattebo run rather than kneeling and trusting Zvada.

Harbaugh called right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), rookie cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck) day to day. Asked if cornerback Paulson Adebo's practice window to return from injured reserve would open this week, Harbaugh said only, "We'll see."

230 — Losses in 230 games by the Giants since 1970 when trailing by 14 or more points in the final eight minutes of regulation, until Sunday. They are now 0-230-1 in those situations.

Players who have taken issue with oddsmakers making the Giants underdogs can again use that as motivation. The Saints opened as 2 1/2-point road favorites.

articles.title: "He was the absent father": Tom Brady's biographer reveals why Gisele Bündchen may have felt sacrificed
articles.summary: Tom Brady built a legendary NFL career through discipline, sacrifice and an unmatched drive to win.
articles.body: Tom Brady built a legendary NFL career through discipline, sacrifice and an unmatched drive to win. But according to his new biographer, those same qualities may have come at a personal cost. Lars Anderson believes Brady's dedication to football played a major role in the breakdown of his 13-year marriage to Gisele Bündchen. In an exclusive interview with PEOPLE, Anderson questioned whether the former couple shared an equal partnership, suggesting that Brady's demanding career and time away from home placed pressure on their family life.Tom Brady's football career reportedly strained his marriage to Gisele BündchenAnderson, author of Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, believes the balance between Brady's professional ambitions and family responsibilities was a key issue in the couple's relationship.“She sacrificed a lot for him and there was never an equal balance,” Anderson speculates.He added, “It was the fact that he was gone, that he was the absent father,” before making his view clear: “And it was football that caused that.”Brady and Bündchen confirmed their divorce in October 2022 after 13 years of marriage. They share two children, Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13, and continue to co-parent them.However, Bündchen previously pushed back against claims that she forced Brady to choose between his family and football. In a 2023 Vanity Fair interview, she described those reports as “very hurtful” and “the craziest thing I’ve ever heard.”Her comments suggested that the split was more complicated than a single disagreement over his NFL career.Anderson also pointed to Brady's absence from the 2016 Rio Olympics, where Bündchen walked the runway during the opening ceremony. He questioned why the quarterback did not travel to support her, despite acknowledging the demands of his football schedule.The author also revealed that Brady missed 11 days of training camp in 2022 in what he described as a last-ditch effort to save the marriage. Even that break, however, could not prevent their eventual separation.Gisele Bündchen reflects on divorce as Tom Brady moves forwardAnderson also questioned the couple's compatibility beyond their shared fame. “If you drill down a little deeper...other than being famous, what did they really have in common?” he asks.He praised Bündchen's interests and influence on Brady, noting her knowledge of fashion, travel and nutrition. His comments suggest that their differences may have extended beyond the time Brady spent on the football field.Despite the painful separation, Bündchen has expressed goodwill towards her former husband. “Listen, I have always cheered for [Tom], and I would continue forever… If there’s one person I want to be the happiest in the world, it’s him, believe me. I want him to achieve and to conquer. I want all his dreams to come true. That’s what I want, really, from the bottom of my heart.”A source also told PEOPLE that Bündchen feels grateful for their years together and is no longer bitter about the divorce.Brady retired from the NFL in February 2023 after 23 seasons and seven Super Bowl victories.
