articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr. Sends Message to Texans Fans in New Video After Cardinals Trade
articles.summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. is ready to get to work for the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. is ready to get to work for the Houston Texans.

"What's up H-Town," the wide receiver said in a video posted Monday. "It's Marvin Harrison Jr. here. I'm super excited to get to work and be a part of a great organization."

The video comes after the Arizona Cardinals traded Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round draft pick to the Texans in exchange for a second- and seventh-rounder in the 2027 draft.

This could be a much-needed change of scenery for Harrison.

After all, he was the Big Ten Offensive Player of the Year and a two-time All-American during his collegiate career at Ohio State. The son of Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison seemed like a lock to be a productive NFL player, and the Cardinals responded by selecting him with the No. 4 overall pick of the 2024 draft.

He flashed his overall potential as a rookie with 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns but saw those numbers drop to 41 catches for 608 yards and four scores during his second season.

Things seemed to be trending in an even worse direction at the start of the 2026 campaign, as Harrison failed to surpass the 40-yard mark in any of his first four games. While the 1-4 Cardinals with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback aren't exactly loaded with game-changing talent to make life easier for him, it was still a stunning lack of production for a top-five pick.

For one, he is reunited with Ohio State teammate C.J. Stroud. The duo led the Buckeyes to the College Football Playoff and already have chemistry in place before Harrison even steps on the field for the Texans.

What's more, the AFC South team needs reliable wide receiver options outside of Nico Collins. With Jayden Higgins out for the season and Tank Dell still working his way back, there is an opening for Harrison to step right in and take advantage of the additional space when defenders are too focused on Collins.

It's not a surprise, then, that he seems excited to start with his new team.

articles.title: Why are Tom Brady and Bill Belichick facing backlash? New England Patriots legends miss 25th-anniversary Super Bowl reunion as Giants appearance raises questions
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Bill Belichick helped build the New England Patriots into an NFL dynasty.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Bill Belichick helped build the New England Patriots into an NFL dynasty. However, their absence from the team's 25th-anniversary celebration of its first Super Bowl title has drawn criticism. The backlash grew after Belichick attended a reunion with the New York Giants just eight days earlier. For Patriots fans, the issue is not just about two legends missing an event. It is also about the small gesture they could have made to honor the team that changed NFL history.The Patriots celebrated their Super Bowl XXXVI championship on Oct. 11, 2026, before facing the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium. Former players returned for the occasion, but Brady and Belichick did not attend or send video messages. Their absence became a talking point on Boston sports radio, where hosts questioned why the two central figures could not spare a few seconds to acknowledge their former teammates. Why Tom Brady and Bill Belichick are facing criticism over the Patriots reunionThe criticism gained momentum on 98.5 The Sports Hub after hosts Michael Felger, Tony Massarotti and Jim Murray discussed the missing Patriots legends. Murray argued that a short phone-recorded message would have been enough to recognize the anniversary."All it takes is two seconds. Just turn that phone around, film a video, send it off to someone at the Patriots," Murray said on the show, as the hosts discussed the October 11 celebration.The point was simple. Neither man needed to attend the ceremony in person to acknowledge the achievement. A brief greeting could have recognized the players who helped New England win its first Super Bowl and begin one of the NFL's greatest dynasties.Brady led the Patriots to a 20-17 victory over the St. Louis Rams in Super Bowl XXXVI on February 3, 2002. The win marked his first Super Bowl title and Belichick's first as New England's head coach. It also began a partnership that produced six championships together.That history made their absence especially noticeable. The celebration also honored kicker Adam Vinatieri, whose 48-yard field goal sealed the Super Bowl victory as time expired. Bill Belichick's Giants reunion adds another layer to the debateBelichick's recent appearance at a New York Giants reunion gave the discussion an extra edge. On October 3, 2026, he attended a dinner marking the 40th anniversary of the Giants' first Super Bowl championship, won during the 1986 season.Belichick served as the Giants' defensive coordinator from 1985 to 1990 and played a key role in their championship success. He attended the dinner after North Carolina, where he now coaches, lost to Notre Dame.The contrast prompted questions about why he could make time for the Giants but not take part in the Patriots' celebration eight days later. Still, neither Belichick nor Brady publicly explained their absence in the material surrounding the event, so their reasons remain unclear.Their past comments about each other also show that their relationship cannot be reduced to a rivalry over credit. On his podcast in 2023, Brady rejected the familiar debate over who deserved more recognition for New England's success."From my standpoint, I think it's always such a stupid conversation to say, 'Brady vs. Belichick' because, in my mind, that's not what a partnership is about," Brady said during the podcast discussion.Belichick also praised their working relationship during Brady's retirement podcast, recalling their football conversations and the respect they shared.Meanwhile, New England's anniversary ceremony went ahead on October 11. Joe Andruzzi carried two American flags onto the field, recalling his gesture after the September 11 attacks, while Vinatieri received his Pro Football Hall of Fame Ring of Excellence at halftime.The Patriots lost 45-17 to the Raiders that day, but the celebration still honored the team that started their championship era. articles.title: Bills-Rams delivered every ounce of Super Bowl LXI preview talk as overtime thriller deserves a rematch
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills outlasted the Los Angeles Rams, 37-34, in overtime after a blocked field goal and Tyler Bass' clutch kick sealed the wild finish.
articles.body: All week, the talk surrounding "Monday Night Football" between the Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams was the potential that this would be a preview for Super Bowl LXI. If this does indeed come to fruition, football fans will be mighty happy because this game was cinema in Inglewood on Monday night. A back-and-forth battle that saw 35 total fourth-quarter points, an overtime period filled with clutch plays, and more led the Bills to beat the Rams, 37-34, to improve to 4-1. The Rams fell to 2-3, a record nobody predicted through their first five games, but they are still a top NFC contender. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE In a game filled with offensive fireworks from both Josh Allen and Matthew Stafford, it was Rams defensive captain Nate Landman who came through with the most important play of the game in overtime. Allen and the Bills got right into Rams territory on the opening drive thanks to Khalil Shakir’s 57-yard catch-and-run on second-and-long. On the very next play, James Cook, who had two touchdowns but a fumble earlier in the game, wasn’t cautious with the football when he got the handoff from Allen. Landman punched at the ball, knocked it clean out of Cook’s arms, and his teammate landed on it. Instead of the Bills getting the potential game-winning score, Stafford and the Rams had a chance to go downfield and win it all thanks to Landman’s efforts. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Stafford did just that, using his star receiver Puka Nacua, who exploded for 17 catches on 25 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown, to get into field goal range for kicker Harrison Mevis to try a 48-yard field goal for the win. But just when it seemed one team would finally come away with the win and get the final word, the other team stepped up. The Rams have dealt with special teams woes in recent seasons, and Mevis, who had missed a 50-yarder earlier in the game, had his game-winning field goal blocked. The game remained tied, and the Bills’ offense breathed a sigh of relief knowing they could rectify Cook’s mistake. Allen took matters into his own hands, rushing for 32 yards on the drive and getting well within field goal range for Tyler Bass to get his shot at glory. The snap was clean, the kick was true, and the Bills celebrated a hard-fought victory that had football fans thinking about the Martin Scorsese "ABSOLUTE CINEMA" meme (if you don’t know that one, look it up). This game truly had it all, especially in the fourth quarter where, just to get to overtime, Stafford had to lead his third straight touchdown drive with 1:39 left on the clock and one timeout. He didn’t even need the timeout, as he found Davante Adams for his second touchdown of the game on a perfect route that left him wide open. Rams head coach Sean McVay elected to go for the tie with an extra point instead of going for a two-point conversion. He had tried earlier at that, but the Rams failed to convert after Stafford was sacked. In the box score, Allen threw for 210 yards with one touchdown and one interception, while rushing for a game-high 121 yards on just 10 carries with his score. Cook finished with 111 yards on the ground with his two touchdowns, while both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum scored for the Rams. From the stars showing up under the bright L.A. lights to the beautiful scoring dance between these two high-octane offenses, to key plays flipping momentum left and right, this game deserves another meeting for the Vince Lombardi Trophy. articles.title: Josh Allen clinches first overtime win of NFL career as Buffalo Bills beat Los Angeles Rams in thriller
articles.summary: Josh Allen rushes for 121 yards, passes for 210 yards and accounts for two touchdowns as the Buffalo Bills beat the Los Angeles Rams in overtime; watch the Jacksonville Jaguars face the Houston Texans in the final NFL London game of the season at Wembley, live on Sky Sports from 2pm Sunday
articles.body:
Allen passed for 210 yards and rushed for 121 more for the Bills (4-1), who rallied to win a frantic game befitting the teams with the NFL's last two MVPs at quarterback.

The Bills appeared to be in trouble after James Cook fumbled early in OT, but Allen got another chance - and he finally won an overtime game for the first time in his career while besting Matthew Stafford, who passed for 383 yards and three touchdowns.

"That's the beautiful thing about football: You get another drive," Allen said. "You get another game. All you can do is keep moving forward. You're hoping someone on defense or special teams can make a play, and that's what happened. Greg Rousseau made a play."

Passing: Josh Allen, 12/19, 210 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Rushing: Josh Allen, 10 carries, 121 yards, 1 TD

Receiving: Khalil Shakir, 3 catches, 80 yards

Passing: Matthew Stafford, 40/54, 383 yards, 3 TDs

Rushing: Kyren Williams, 16 carries, 49 yards, 1 TD

Receiving: Puka Nacua, 17 catches, 138 yards, 1 TD

Cook scored his second touchdown with 1:39 left in regulation for Buffalo, but Kyren Williams scored on a one-yard surge with four seconds left to force overtime. The Bills began by driving deep into Rams territory, but Aaron Donald recovered Cook's fumble after Nate Landman punched it out.

Stafford drove the Rams to the Buffalo 30, but Harrison Mevis missed his second field goal attempt of the night when Rousseau got a piece of it.

"The kicking game, with our PAT, field goal [unit] - not even close to good enough," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "It cost us the game tonight. I'm going to evaluate everything."

Allen then made scrambles of 19 and 13 yards before rookie Bills coach Joe Brady elected to try the field goal on second down with nearly two minutes still on the clock. Bass blasted his kick and ran away to celebrate before the officials signalled it good.

"The confidence I had in T-Bass was, 'Hey, 45 yards, he's going to make this kick,'" Brady said.

Allen got more than 100 of his yards rushing on scrambles, repeatedly escaping the pocket and rendering useless the Rams' tenacious secondary coverage.

"When it's there, it's there," Allen said. "I don't want to make a living on that, I understand that, but I do know how much of a backbreaker that can be on a defense when you think you're in pretty good coverage. I felt like there was some room to manoeuvre there and keep the chains moving."

Cook rushed for 111 yards before a costly fumble added to the Bills' recent ball-security concerns. Buffalo improved to 4-1, marking its sixth 4-1 start in the past eight seasons.

Puka Nacua hauled in a career-high 17 receptions for 138 yards and a touchdown for the Rams (2-3), who have started below 500 after five games for the fourth time in five seasons.

Rams head coach Sean McVay was furious with another special-teams collapse and also questioned his own decision to call a conservative play on third-and-5 before Harrison Mevis missed a long field-goal attempt in overtime.

"I wish I would have had a better play call and gone for it, got it tighter," McVay said. "I'm sick right now with myself, and I'm so proud of that group. This is the tough part of sports, but I'm proud of that team. I'm proud of the way we battled, and I'm sick that we came up short."

Buffalo's superior special-teams play and Josh Allen's relentless effort proved decisive as the Bills edged the Rams in another high-scoring shootout. Their previous meeting in December 2024 also produced a classic, with the teams combining for 902 total yards in Los Angeles' 44-42 victory.

After Davante Adams hauled in his second touchdown catch with 7:14 remaining, capping a game that featured six consecutive lead changes, Allen led Buffalo on a 71-yard drive, using two scrambles to exploit the Rams' defence.

James Cook then scored the go-ahead touchdown. Matthew Stafford responded by completing six of seven passes to move Los Angeles to the Buffalo 1-yard line, where the Rams opted against using a timeout before Kyren Williams punched in the tying score.

Adams' second touchdown also brought him level with Larry Fitzgerald for the sixth-most touchdown receptions in NFL history, with 121. Blake Corum added a rushing touchdown, while tight end Tyler Higbee caught five passes for 83 yards.

For Buffalo, Keon Coleman caught Allen's only touchdown pass of the night.

articles.title: ‘This Is Shameless,’ ‘You’re Better Than That’ — NFL Fans Unimpressed as Pat McAfee Calls Josh Allen’s INT an ‘Arm Punt’ on MNF
articles.summary: Josh Allen’s eyebrow-raising interception meant Pat McAfee’s reaction became a talking point of its own on Monday Night Football. The ESPN analyst called it...
articles.body:
Josh Allen's eyebrow-raising interception meant Pat McAfee's reaction became a talking point of its own on Monday Night Football. The ESPN analyst called it an "arm punt," a phrase that some fans saw as a reasonable football description, and others viewed as an excuse for a costly mistake.

This split spilled onto social media, where viewers questioned whether McAfee would have described another quarterback's interception the same way.

NFL Fans Criticize Pat McAfee for Calling Josh Allen's INT an 'Arm Punt'

With the Buffalo Bills leading late in the first half, Allen threw a third-down pass that Los Angeles Rams defensive back Jaylen Watson intercepted near midfield.

McAfee's reaction to the interception quickly drew attention when he described Allen's deep third-down throw as an "arm punt," prompting some viewers to accuse the ESPN personality of downplaying the turnover.

An "arm punt" has been used to describe a deep pass on third down that gets intercepted but can still function like a punt by pushing the opposing offense back.

McAfee's comment drew criticism from viewers who believed the explanation softened a costly decision by one of the NFL's biggest stars.

One account shared the clip on X and wrote , "THIS IS SHAMELESS."

The response showed frustration among fans who believe prominent quarterbacks receive gentler treatment from national broadcasters. One viewer questioned the wording directly, posting , "Y'all hear Pat McAfee calling it an arm punt??? Can't make this up."

For some, the issue was not whether the phrase existed in the NFL rule book, but whether it was appropriate in that moment.

Another fan appealed to McAfee's reputation for unfiltered commentary, writing , "Pat McAfee Show, did you just say arm punt from Josh Allen, instead of interception? Come on, man. You're better than that."

There was a football argument behind McAfee's description. Allen's interception came on third-and-6 from Buffalo's 16-yard line, and Watson's return gave the Rams possession at their own 43. The turnover produced a field-position result similar to a punt, although it remained an interception on the official stat sheet.

The criticism also extended to the wider broadcast. Play-by-play announcer Joe Buck described the interception as being "almost like a punt," prompting one viewer to accuse ESPN's commentators of protecting Allen.

The fan wrote , "Now Pat McAfee out here calling it an arm punt. Jesus, this guy gets total protection from his media partners."

Not everyone viewed McAfee's remark as serious analysis. One fan offered a more charitable interpretation, saying , "I thought he said it tongue-in-cheek."

This distinction matters because McAfee, a former NFL punter, has used his playing experience and informal delivery to build his media profile. Some viewers saw the comment as a joke rather than an attempt to excuse Allen's decision.

Others defended the terminology itself, separating its football meaning from the controversy surrounding its use. One fan wrote , "'Arm Punt' is a situational description. Been around for a long time. And I see Pat McAfee just said the exact same thing I did."

Another supported that argument, adding , "Hardly a new term… I remember hearing it on VSiN several years ago."
